relations.subject: sgw:shared-bucket-access-setting
relations.object: true will be mandatory in a future release; false will not be supported
relations.evidence: Setting this property to `true` will be required in a future release, and `false` will not be supported.

relations.subject: sgw:shared-bucket-access-setting
relations.evidence: Enabling shared bucket access on your existing deployment is **not** reversible.

relations.subject: sgw:shared-bucket-access-setting
relations.object: Couchbase Server 6.0 known issue MB-41255 (rebalance/replica-write failures on deleted or expired Xattr documents)
relations.evidence: The known issue can cause re-balance failures and/or failed replica writes of deleted or expired documents that use Xattrs.

relations.subject: storage:extended-attribute
relations.evidence: There are currently three types of XATTRS: User, System and Virtual.

relations.subject: storage:tombstone
relations.evidence: Shares lifetime with the document metadata - when a document is deleted, system xattrs are preserved with the tombstone.

relations.subject: storage:extended-attribute
relations.evidence: Are accessible from SQL++ in Couchbase Server using the `().xattrs` property.

relations.subject: sgw:sync-metadata
relations.evidence: Sync Gateway \[[1](#%5Ffootnotedef%5F1 "View footnote.")\] creates the metadata it needs by abstracting it from the SDK or SQL++ applications reading and writing data directly to Couchbase Server buckets.

relations.subject: sgw:sync-metadata
relations.evidence: The `_raw` endpoint (/db/\_raw/{docid}) on Sync Gateway's Admin REST API returns both the document and its associated mobile metadata.

relations.subject: sgw:sync-metadata
relations.object: structure can change at any time; must not drive application business logic
relations.evidence: The sync metadata is maintained internally by Sync Gateway and its structure can change at any time. It should not be used to drive business logic of applications.

relations.subject: sgw:sync-metadata
relations.object: direct SQL++ querying of sync metadata is unsupported in production
relations.evidence: The direct use of the SQL++ query or modifying the internal sync metadata contents to drive the business logic is unsupported and must not be used in production environments.

relations.subject: sgw:tombstone
relations.evidence: To ensure tombstones are synced with clients, you should set the server's metadata purge interval based on your expected replication frequency

relations.subject: sgw:tombstone
relations.object: not retained indefinitely under shared bucket access; purged per Server metadata purge interval
relations.evidence: Note that, with bucket-sharing enabled, [tombstone revision![glossary icon](../_images/icons/glossaryIconImage2.png)](../glossary.md#tombstone-revision)s are **not** retained indefinitely; they are purged based on the server's _metadata purge interval_.

relations.subject: sgw:attachment
relations.evidence: Use Sync Gateway's REST API's [/{db}/{docid}/{attachment}](../rest-api/rest-api-admin.md#/attachment) endpoints to manage attachments and blob data; you cannot use Couchbase Server SDKs to do this directly.

relations.subject: sgw:import-docs-setting
relations.evidence: Note that `import_docs` only takes effect if the `enabled_shared_bucket_access` is set to `true`.

relations.subject: sgw:import-docs-setting
relations.evidence: The `import_docs` parameter defaults to `true`, implying that, by default, all nodes in a cluster participate in import processing.

relations.subject: sgw:import-docs-setting
relations.evidence: The `import_docs` parameter defaults to `false` and must be explicitly set to `true`.

relations.subject: sgw:import-docs-setting
relations.object: Enterprise Edition (for sharded, high-availability import processing)
relations.evidence: In _Enterprise Edition_, import processing work is sharded across all Sync Gateway nodes with import enabled. This implies that if one of the nodes fail, the failed shard is automatically picked up by the remaining nodes in the cluster.

relations.subject: sgw:import-docs-setting
relations.evidence: In _Community Edition_, there is no sharding of import across the nodes participating in the import processing. Each import node processes all server mutations.

relations.subject: sgw:import-docs-setting
relations.object: workload isolation (import_docs: false isolates client-facing nodes from import nodes)
relations.evidence: This configuration is specifically recommended for workload isolation: to isolate import nodes from the client-facing nodes. Workload isolation may be preferable in deployments with high write throughput.

notable_absence.finding: This is the page most directly comparable to XDCR/DCP mechanics per the round brief, and it was read specifically to check for a drawn comparison between Sync-Gateway<->Server sync and XDCR or DCP replication. The word 'DCP' never appears on this page. 'XDCR' appears in exactly one CAUTION admonition unrelated to mechanism comparison: 'Bi-directional XDCR is only supported in Sync Gateway 4.0. For earlier versions, upgrade to 4.0 to use bi-directional XDCR.' This is a version-compatibility caveat about Sync Gateway's own native bi-directional XDCR feature (see the reconciliation-corrected relation above, now sgw:bidirectional-xdcr rather than xdcr:active-active-with-app-services), not a statement that Sync Gateway's own change-detection mechanism is XDCR-like or DCP-based. One further near-miss: the generic XATTR-behaviour bullet 'Are stored and replicated along with the associated document in both intra-cluster and XDCR replication' describes Couchbase Server's general XATTR replication behaviour (a storage:extended-attribute fact), not Sync Gateway's own sync mechanism - it was NOT treated as an SGW-uses-DCP or SGW-uses-XDCR relation, since the page never makes that specific claim.

cross_component_finding: The page's XATTR-based sync-metadata mechanism is the load-bearing bridge between two already-promoted concepts, sgw:tombstone and sgw:meta-xattr-arg (the sync-function's read side of the same storage): mobile metadata lives in a System XATTR that 'shares lifetime with the document metadata' and survives into the tombstone, while sgw:meta-xattr-arg (from round 27) is how the sync function reads XATTR-sourced values back out. This page adds the write/storage side: Sync Gateway itself writes this metadata via XATTRs, not via the sync function.
cross_product_finding: Resolved during round 28 reconciliation (see the corrected relation above and its reconciliation_note): this page's 'Bi-directional XDCR is only supported in Sync Gateway 4.0' is not a terminology variance on xdcr:active-active-with-app-services's 'Requires Server 7.6.6+, App Services 4.0+' - it is a different, on-prem-native feature (sgw:bidirectional-xdcr) that this round's server-compatibility/ batch independently promotes, gated at Server 7.6.5+ rather than 7.6.6+ and framed with no App Services dependency at all. The two xdcr:active-active-with-app-services and sgw:bidirectional-xdcr concepts remain correctly unmerged per compatibility.json's own no-silent-merge reasoning.
